newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CZECH CHAMPS HAVE FOUR BANNED, FINNS CRASH.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CZECH CHAMPS HAVE FOUR BANNED, FINNS CRASH.

text.p: Title holders the Czech Republic fought back into the medal hunt but had four players banned while Finland's challenge ended at the world ice hockey championship on Wednesday.
Finland, playing in a new 14,000-seat state-of-the-art arena that was rushed to completion for the championship, were booed off the ice after losing 5-2 to Sweden.
Pre-tournament favourites Finland will now wrap up play on Friday in a meaningless game against the United States, who still cling to an outside chance of a place in the bronze medal match.
Earlier in the day, the Czech Republic beat Canada 5-3 in a hard-hitting contest that ended in a bench clearing brawl, a total of eight players suspended and coaches trading insults.
A vocal sell-out crowd, cheering wildly each time the Finns touched the puck, was quickly silenced when the Swedes seized a 2-0 first-period lead on goals by Jonas Hoglund and Per Eklund.
But the party picked up in the second when Ville Peltonen put Finland back into the game with a pair of powerplay goals.
The celebrations were short lived, however, as Michael Nylander and Jorgen Jonsson restored Sweden's two-goal advantage before the end of the period.
"I don't know why the players were so nervous, everything seemed fine this morning," said Curt Lindstrom, who will resign as Finland coach at the end of the tournament.
"Maybe we were so eager, we wanted so much...we tried everything. We fought like hell but..."
Vladimir Vujtek hit a hat-trick as the Czech Republic kept alive their hopes of a second title with a fight-filled win over Canada.

Vujtek, who had the only goal of the second period to put the Czechs 3-2 ahead completed his triple strike when he back-handed the puck over Canadian netminder Sean Burke to open the scoring in the third period.
The Czech's Rostislav Vlach and Canada's Don Sweeney traded goals before the game degenerated into a bench-clearing brawl.
Pressure and tempers had been building the entire period until they finally boiled over with about 40 seconds to play.
Several skirmishes broke out all over the ice, even netminders Burke and Roman Cechmanek were drawn into the fray, skating the length of the ice to confront each other.
Referee Peter Andersson of Sweden handed out a total of 244 minutes in penalties, including eight game misconducts, four to each team.
Canada will be without Rob Blake, Owen Nolan, Travis Green and Shean Donovan for their key game against Russia on Friday.
The Czechs will have to overcome Sweden on Thursday without Libor Prochazka, Robert Lang, Jiri Slegr and Vujtek.

The hard feelings spilled over into the post-game news conference, with Czech coach Slavomir Lerner accusing Canada's Andy Murray of being a cheat and the worst coach the country has had in seven years.
"If he says I'm the weakest coach, my question to him is if he is such a strong coach why is Ivan Hlinka behind the bench as a coach," said Murray in response to the accusations.
"He called us Canadian cheaters, that I had no class and now I know why the NHL players in Calgary where he was an assistant have no respect for him.
"One thing we have to recognise is that the Czechs are the dirtiest players in the world.
"Anyone who has watched them play can see their stick work. A Canadian is a tough hockey player, a Czech is a dirty hockey player."
The final period ruined what until then had been an entertaining, wide open contest.
Tampa Bay Ligthnings Rob Zamunner had scored twice for Canada in the opening period while Vujtek notched his first and set up Martin Prochazka for another.

The win leaves Sweden alone at the top of the standings with six points followed by Russia on five and the Czechs and Canada both on four. With one game remaing for every team, the U.S. are on three and Finland two.
